text:
Sam Lee: alerting — cert1 region heartbeats vanished around 1939001108. control-plane gRPC pings failing.
Alex Rivera: seeing 5xx on regional API gateway, health checks show all backends Unhealthy.
infra-bot: ALERT: region_cert1_heartbeat_missing -> 1939001109 :rotating_light:
Priya Patel: @oncall-east (Alex) can you confirm BGP/session level or API plane? I can start traffic shift if we need.
Alex Rivera: quick check — BGP sessions to cert1 edge still up, but our control-plane probes show tcp 504 to kube-apiserver. lb logs:
```
[1939001109] lb-proxy: connect timeout to 10.0.5.12:443 (apiserver)
[1939001110] healthcheck: 0/6 healthy
```
Miguel Santos: looks like control-plane nodes are unresponsive. Could be firewall or cluster control-plane crash. Who's the oncall infra? @Jin
Jin Park: I'm oncall, looking now. Can you dump recent kubelet logs from cert1-control-0?
Sam Lee: posted logs gist -> https://internal.gists/redwood/abcd1234 shows repeated `evicting pods` and `watch cache timeout` within 10s.
Nora Gupta: start traffic fallback to standby region? We should avoid mass failover unless necessary — prefer gradual route weights shift to eu-west-standby.
Priya Patel: Agreed. Plan: 1) pin critical customers to dedicated Dedicated pools in other regions 2) shift ~20% traffic by route policy to eu-west-standby, monitor errors 3) escalate to full failover if errors >2% for 5m.
Alex Rivera: executing weight update now (route policy id: rp-ops-207). Command:
```
redwood-routectl set-weight --policy rp-ops-207 --region cert1 --weight 80
redwood-routectl set-weight --policy rp-ops-207 --region eu-west-standby --weight 20
```
deploy-bot: route policy rp-ops-207 updated (1939001138) :white_check_mark:
Miguel Santos: checking GPU fleets — dedicated pools in cert1 show kubelet OOM evictions on gpu-node-*. GPUs online but pods being killed, so capacity degraded even if HW up.
Sam Lee: that's bad — workloads will get queued and latency spikes will cascade. Priya, do we want to prioritize stateless generation requests for now?
Priya Patel: yes — enable promo routing to prefer stateless model variants and pause batch jobs. Patch quick policy:
```
/ops/policies/prioritize_stateless.sh --region cert1 --enable
```
Jin Park: I'm SSHing to control-plane node, collecting system journal and checking for recent kernel OOMs.
Nora Gupta: notify CS and set status page to "degraded service in cert1, partial failover in progress". I'll craft incident note.
Sam Lee: created incident page -> https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1939001111
Alex Rivera: monitoring metrics — p50 latency up 2.5x in cert1, error rate 9%. eu-west-standby traffic stable so far.
infra-bot: escalated to PagerDuty team: infra-core (1939001145)
Jin Park: kernel logs show memory pressure and cgroup eviction at 1939001106. Appears a bad kube-proxy upgrade + a cron causing memory leak.
Miguel Santos: rollback kube-proxy by reverting daemonset to image v1.20.3-rc: `kubectl rollout undo ds/kube-proxy -n kube-system` — proceeding.
Priya Patel: good. Keep rolling weight updates incremental. If control-plane recovers, we can rehydrate traffic.
Alex Rivera: rollback complete at 1939001189. Observability shows pod restarts decreasing.
Sam Lee: what about storage/etcd health?
Jin Park: etcd cluster still partially healthy but leader elections increased. I'm forcing snapshot and pausing heavy writes.
Nora Gupta: posting customer comms draft now. tagging legal for regulated customers.
Sam Lee: next steps: hold traffic shift at 20% for 10m, watch error budget, then decide full cutover or restore. Everyone on this thread pls ack when you see the change.
Priya Patel: ack — I'm watching model routing and cost impacts.
Miguel Santos: ack — GPU pools observed, batching paused for cert1.
Alex Rivera: ack — watching gateway.
Jin Park: ack — control-plane remediation ongoing.
Nora Gupta: ack — comms live.
infra-bot: incident log appended: playbook:region-vanish -> step traffic-shift (1939001235)
Sam Lee: good work team. We'll update after the 10m window.
